Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has expressed confidence that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, will not win Lagos in the 2027 election as he did in 2023. Fashola said the All Progressives Congress was “blindsided” by Obi’s victory in the state during the last presidential election, adding that the party had learnt from the experience. He spoke on Friday during an exclusive interview on Arise Television, where he was asked whether he was confident that Obi, who is returning to the ballot on the NDC platform, would repeat his 2023 performance in Lagos. “Yes, I am,” Fashola replied when asked if he was confident Obi would not win the state again. Explaining the reason for his confidence, the former governor said the APC had quickly recovered from its defeat at the presidential level by winning the subsequent governorship election in the state. It won’t happen again. “Lagos didn’t look like a battleground at the time. And I think it is important just to say that they quickly claimed the result of Lagos, but denied the results in other places,” he said. The interviewer challenged the claim, noting that Obi’s supporters had also alleged that more than 100,000 votes were taken away from them in Lagos. No Nigerian should be victimised for supporting Obi – Obidient Movement OK Movement faction withdraws support for Obi, NDC Tinubu’s certificate controversy a needless distraction – Fashola Fashola dismissed the issue as history, urging voters to focus on the January 16, 2027 presidential election and support the APC. “That is now history. What is upon us should be January 16 and why people must vote APC for all of the work that has been done, for the leadership that has been shown, for the ability to work with others and the resilience to confront problems,” he said. He also criticised politicians who move from one political party to another when they encounter resistance within their parties. In the 2023 presidential election, Obi, who contested on the Labour Party platform, polled 582,454 votes in Lagos, defeating the APC candidate, Bola Tinubu, who secured 572,606 votes. The result was notable because Lagos was Tinubu’s political base and had been governed by the APC since 1999. Tinubu, however, went on to win the 2023 presidential election nationally, while the APC retained Lagos in the governorship election held in March of the same year. The 2027 presidential election is scheduled to hold on January 16, with Obi set to contest on the NDC platform alongside other candidates , including incumbent President Bola Tinubu of the APC.
